ai.description: This slender snake reaches 70 cm. It is brown or grey with white crossbars and a distinct white, Y-shaped mark on the head. It features enlarged, fang-like anterior teeth and a flattened snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Common Wolf Snake is best identified by the distinct white or yellowish "collar" or series of white cross-bands on its head and neck, which are absent in similar vipers.
ai.habitat: The Common Wolf Snake inhabits diverse environments, ranging from lowland tropical forests and scrublands to urban gardens and human dwellings, up to 2,000 meters altitude.
ai.behavior: The Common Wolf Snake is primarily nocturnal, using its specialized, recurved teeth to securely grip and consume geckos and skinks during its active nightly hunts.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Common Wolf Snake is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–11 eggs. Breeding typically occurs throughout the year, with peaks often observed during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Common Wolf Snake is widespread across the Indian subcontinent, occurring from sea level up to 2,000 meters throughout most Indian states and neighboring countries.
